assertion_results.text: Version impact table shows mixed results: 2.1.x versions marked YES (affected) and 2.2.x versions marked NO (not affected) based on lock file evidence
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md contains a table where 2.1.0 and 2.1.1 are marked YES (h2 0.4.5, < 0.4.8) and all 2.2.x versions (2.2.0 through 2.2.4) are marked NO (h2 >= 0.4.8). The evidence is based on lock file analysis at pinned commits (e.g., 'git show <tag>:Cargo.lock'). The Stream Impact Summary explicitly states '2.1.x: ALL versions affected' and '2.2.x: No versions affected'.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction includes only the actually affected versions (2.1.x versions), not the unaffected 2.2.x versions (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md Step 3.2 shows: 'Current Affects Versions: [RHTPA 2.1.0, RHTPA 2.2.0]' corrected to 'Proposed Affects Versions: [RHTPA 2.1.0, RHTPA 2.1.1]'. RHTPA 2.2.0 is removed (ships h2 0.4.8, at fix threshold) and RHTPA 2.1.1 is added (ships h2 0.4.5, vulnerable). The proposed Jira update and comment confirm only 2.1.x versions remain.

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks are created only for the affected stream (2.1.x), not for 2.2.x which already ships the patched version (Step 8 Case A scoping)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md creates exactly two tasks, both scoped to stream 2.1.x: Task 1 'Upstream Backport (Stream 2.1.x)' targeting release/0.3.z, and Task 2 'Downstream Propagation (Stream 2.1.x)'. The decision tree states: 'create remediation tasks for stream 2.1.x only. Stream 2.2.x is not affected and requires no remediation.' No tasks are created for 2.2.x.

assertion_results.text: The analysis treats the issue as unscoped (no stream suffix) and checks ALL versions across all streams (Step 1 Stream scope resolution, unscoped path)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md explicitly states: 'Stream scope: Unscoped -- no stream suffix present; issue covers all streams' and 'The issue summary... contains no stream suffix... treated as unscoped -- it covers all configured version streams (2.1.x and 2.2.x).' version-impact.md checks all 7 versions across both streams: 2.1.0, 2.1.1, 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4.

assertion_results.text: Cross-stream impact notice is NOT generated because the issue is unscoped — it covers all streams by definition (Step 8 Case B applies only to scoped issues)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md decision tree states: 'Case A (cross-stream impact)? SKIPPED -- unscoped issues cover all streams by definition; Case A applies only to scoped issues.' The pre-creation checklist confirms: 'Cross-stream coverage: N/A -- issue is unscoped, Case A is skipped. No preemptive tasks needed.' No cross-stream impact notice appears anywhere in the outputs.
